poster_title: Multimodal Retrieval-Reflection-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Based VQA
authors: Tao Zhang, Ziqi Zhang, Zongyang Ma, Yuxin Chen, Zhongang Qi, Chunfeng Yuan, Bing Li, Junfu Pu, Yuxuan Zhao, Zehua Xie, Jin Ma, Ying Shan, Weiming Hu

panels.headline: MLLMs excel in Visual-dependent VQA but struggle with Knowledge-based VQA.
content: MLLMs perform well in tasks requiring visual information but are limited by their static knowledge scope in Knowledge-based VQA.
Current mRAG methods often introduce unnecessary retrieval, lack of evidence localization, and increased model complexity.
There is a need for a more efficient and effective framework to enhance Knowledge-based VQA capabilities without compromising the strengths of MLLMs.
The proposed mR 2 AG framework aims to address these limitations.
The framework introduces two reflection operations to improve the accuracy and relevance of answers.

panels.headline: MLLMs provide ambiguous and inaccurate responses to Knowledge-based VQA tasks.
content: MLLMs struggle with providing precise answers to Knowledge-based VQA tasks due to their limited and static knowledge scope.
Existing mRAG methods indiscriminately use retrieval, leading to inefficiency and increased model complexity.
There is a lack of explicit evidence localization in current mRAG methods, affecting the quality of generated answers.
The proposed mR 2 AG framework aims to overcome these challenges.
It introduces adaptive retrieval and explicit evidence localization to improve answer accuracy and relevance.

panels.headline: mR 2 AG uses two reflection operations: Retrieval-Reflection and Relevance-Reflection.
content: Retrieval-Reflection determines the necessity of retrieval for a given query, avoiding redundant retrieval calls.
Relevance-Reflection guides the MLLM to locate and utilize relevant evidence from the retrieved content, ensuring accurate answer generation.

panels.headline: Achieved performance gains of 10.6% and 15.5% over previous SOTAs on INFOSEEK test sets.
content: Evaluated on Knowledge-based VQA datasets: INFOSEEK and Encyclopedic-VQA.
Compared with state-of-the-art MLLMs (e.g., GPT-4v/o) and RAG-based MLLMs.
panels.figure_caption: Main results of models with external knowledge on the INFOSEEK dataset.

panels.headline: mR 2 AG significantly improves performance on Knowledge-based VQA tasks.
content: mR 2 AG outperformed SOTAs on the Enc-VQA test set by 2.5% on single-hop questions and 18.2% on multi-answer questions.
The framework demonstrated significant performance improvements while maintaining the base MLLM's capabilities on Visual-dependent tasks.
The effectiveness of mR 2 AG depends on the quality of the retrieved content and the base MLLM's ability to understand and utilize the evidence.
The mR 2 AG-IT dataset was specifically constructed for Knowledge-based VQA tasks, providing a valuable resource for future research.
The proposed framework offers a balanced approach to enhancing Knowledge-based VQA without increasing model complexity.

panels.headline: mR 2 AG effectively addresses the limitations of current mRAG methods.
content: mR 2 AG introduces adaptive retrieval and explicit evidence localization, significantly improving performance on Knowledge-based VQA tasks.
The framework retains the strengths of base MLLMs on Visual-dependent tasks.
The mR 2 AG-IT dataset provides a valuable resource for future research in Knowledge-based VQA.
The proposed method offers a more efficient and effective approach to enhancing Knowledge-based VQA capabilities.
The framework can be applied to other multimodal tasks requiring external knowledge.
